title: Project assurance, project support and change authority
blurb: Explain who is accountable for project assurance, who may carry it out, why project support stays separate from it, and how the board delegates change authority.
question: A senior user delegates user assurance to an operations manager. Who is now accountable for user assurance?

teach.h: Project assurance: the board checking for itself
teach.body: Formally: project board members are accountable for the assurance of their own areas of concern (business, user and supplier), and the board decides how project assurance will be carried out. In plain English: the board cannot rely on the project manager's word alone, so each member arranges independent checks on their part of the project. Assurance is independent of the project manager, not of the project.

Checks, for example
rows: The project stays justified and affordable
teach.caption: Delegating the work of assurance does not move the board member's accountability.

teach.h: Who may carry out project assurance?

children.label: The board member
children.sub: or someone from the wider business, or an external party

children.label: PM, team members, support
children.sub: they cannot assure their own work

teach.caption: Choice depends on who has the knowledge, skills and capacity.

teach.body: Project support provides services such as administrative support, facilitating meetings and workshops, advice on project tools, planning support, and help with risk, issue and change management, including keeping registers and version control. It is the project manager's responsibility but can be delegated, for example to a project office, a supplier or team members.

rows.label: Purpose
values: Services that help run the project

teach.caption: Keeping them apart protects the independence of assurance.

teach.body: The project board is the ultimate authority for requests for change and off-specifications, but it may delegate approval to a change authority (a person or group) or to the project manager, within set limits and usually with a change budget. The arrangement is recorded in the issue management approach and role descriptions and reviewed at each stage boundary.

steps.label: Project board
steps.sub: ultimate authority; sets limits and change budget

steps.label: Project board decides
steps.sub: or escalates if tolerances are threatened

teach.caption: Delegation is about approving changes, not carrying them out.

teach.body: At Pennant Logistics, executive Sara Holt asks a finance business partner to carry out business assurance. Senior user Dev Malik asks the warehouse operations manager to do user assurance, and senior supplier Chris Byrne hires an external engineering consultancy for supplier assurance. Project manager Ana Silva's coordinator keeps the registers as project support. The board delegates change authority to a three-person panel with a £20,000 change budget. Dev remains accountable for user assurance.

teach.text: Traps: (1) Project assurance is NOT quality assurance: one is the board's, the other is independent of the whole PMT. (2) The project manager, team members and project support can never do project assurance. (3) Delegating assurance or change authority does not remove the board's accountability.

items: Board members are accountable for assurance of business, user and supplier areas.
Assurance may be done by the board member, the wider business or an external party, never the PM, team or support.
Project support is the PM's responsibility, can be delegated, and stays separate from assurance.
The board may delegate change authority within limits, ideally with a change budget.

summary: You can now explain how project assurance works and who may and may not carry it out, what project support does and why it is kept separate, and how the board delegates change authority.

A.q: Who is accountable for project assurance of the user area?
A.why: Board members are accountable for assurance of their own area: the senior user for user assurance.

whyNot.0: Project assurance cannot be assigned to the project manager.
whyNot.2: Project support must be kept separate from project assurance.
whyNot.3: The team manager delivers work for the project manager; user assurance is the senior user's accountability as the board member for that area.

A.q: Which person may NOT carry out project assurance?
options: A manager from the wider business
A.why: Project assurance roles cannot be assigned to the project manager, team members or project support.

whyNot.0: Assurance may be selected from an external party.
whyNot.1: Assurance may be appointed from the wider business.
whyNot.2: Board members may carry out assurance of their own area themselves.

A.why: Project support is the project manager's responsibility, though it can be delegated.

whyNot.1: The board is responsible for project assurance, not support.
whyNot.2: The business layer commissions the project and is outside the PMT.
whyNot.3: The senior supplier commits supplier resources; support remains the PM's responsibility even if delegated to a supplier.

B.q: Which statement about project assurance is correct?
options: It is independent of the project management team
It is the project manager's responsibility
It is independent of the project manager
It can be combined with project support
B.why: Project assurance checks the project on the board's behalf, independently of the project manager.

whyNot.0: Independence from the whole PMT describes quality assurance; project assurance is part of the project.
whyNot.1: Project assurance is the board's responsibility.
whyNot.3: Project support must be kept separate from project assurance.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Project support can be delegated to a project office.
2. Delegating assurance moves the board member's accountability.
3. Project support must be kept separate from project assurance.
4. A change authority is the ultimate authority for changes.
B.why: Support can be delegated, for example to a project office (1), and must be kept separate from assurance (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the board member remains accountable when assurance is delegated.
whyNot.2: Both are false: accountability stays with the board member, and the board is the ultimate change authority.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the project board is the ultimate authority; a change authority acts within delegated limits.

B.q: Which statement about a change authority is correct?
options: It sets the change budget for the project board
It is the ultimate authority for every change
It approves changes within limits set by the board
It implements the changes that it has approved
B.why: A change authority is a person or group to whom the board delegates approval of requests for change and off-specifications within limits.

whyNot.0: The board sets the change budget and allocates it with the delegated authority.
whyNot.1: The project board remains the ultimate authority.
whyNot.3: Delegation is about approving changes, not implementing them.

C.q: Who is the ultimate authority for requests for change, and to whom may it delegate approval?
options: Project board; a change authority or the PM
C.why: The project board is the ultimate authority for requests for change and off-specifications and may delegate to a change authority or the PM (10.2.4).

whyNot.0: Authority sits with the board, and support is administrative and kept separate from assurance.
whyNot.1: The board, not the business layer, is the ultimate authority for project changes.
whyNot.2: A change authority holds delegated authority only; the board is the ultimate authority.

C.q: A senior user is too busy to assure user interests and asks a respected operations manager to do it. Who is now accountable for user assurance, and who does the work?
C.why: Where assurance is delegated, the board member remains accountable; the delegate carries out the tasks.

whyNot.1: Delegating the tasks does not transfer the senior user's accountability.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is independent of the PM, who cannot be accountable for it.
whyNot.3: The executive is accountable for business assurance, and the work has been delegated.

options: Project assurance: PM; quality assurance: board
Project assurance: board; quality assurance: business function
Project assurance: business function; quality assurance: PM
Project assurance: support; quality assurance: board
C.why: Project assurance is the board's responsibility; quality assurance is a business or programme function independent of the project management team.

whyNot.0: Project assurance cannot be done by the PM, and quality assurance sits outside the PMT.
whyNot.2: This reverses the two, and quality assurance is independent of the PM.
whyNot.3: Project support cannot do project assurance, and quality assurance is outside the board.

reteach.title: Auditors, admin and a spending limit
reteach.question: In a company, can the person whose work is being audited also be the auditor?

blocks.body: A finance team has auditors who check its work for the directors (project assurance), an admin team that keeps the books tidy for the finance manager (project support), and a committee allowed to approve spending up to a limit (change authority). The auditors must be independent of the finance manager and of the admin team. The directors still answer for the audit, even when they hire the auditors.

blocks.text: The admin team cannot also be the auditors: project support is kept separate from project assurance.

explain.body: Each board member is accountable for assurance of their area: executive for business, senior user for user, senior supplier for supplier.

test.q: Who is accountable for business assurance?
test.why: The executive is accountable for assurance of the business area.

whyNot.0: The senior supplier is accountable for supplier assurance.
whyNot.1: The project manager cannot be given project assurance.
whyNot.3: The business layer is outside the PMT; assurance is the board's responsibility.

explain.body: Assurance tasks can be done by the board member, someone appointed from the wider business or an external party. They cannot be given to the PM, team members or project support.

test.q: Which could carry out supplier assurance?
options: A team member building the product
test.why: Assurance may be selected from an external party with the right knowledge and skills.

whyNot.0: Project assurance cannot be assigned to the project manager.
whyNot.1: Project support must be kept separate from assurance.
whyNot.2: Team members cannot carry out project assurance.

explain.body: Administrative support, meetings and workshops, tool advice, planning support, risk, issue and change administration, registers and version control. The PM's responsibility; may be delegated.

test.q: Which task is typical of project support?
test.why: Project support administers risk, issue and change management, including maintaining registers.

whyNot.1: Independent checks of the business case are business assurance.
whyNot.2: Approving changes is for the board, a change authority or a PM with delegated authority.
whyNot.3: Stage tolerances are set by the project board.

explain.body: The board may delegate approval of changes to a change authority within limits. A change budget should come with it so approved changes can be funded.

test.q: What should accompany delegated change authority so that approved changes can be funded?
test.why: Delegated authority should come with a change budget so approved changes can actually be funded and implemented.

whyNot.0: A risk budget funds risk responses, not approved changes.
whyNot.2: The project mandate starts the project; it does not fund changes.
whyNot.3: A lessons report passes on lessons; it has no funding role.
